bullets.section: Headset I’m using and taking on travel
bullets.title: SHOKZ OpenMeet UC
bullets.note: I’ve been experimenting a lot with headsets that do _not_ go in the ears. While noise-cancelling AirPods and the like are still best for loud environments, I’ve had a few ear infections and a lot of discomfort over the years. These SHOKZ were recommended by polymath [Elan Lee](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzggnC5Jwts), who uses them mostly on his laptop and desktop. I tend to use them when walking and listening to podcasts, or when using [Wispr Flow](https://wisprflow.ai/) to braindump long drafts into a text file, which I then drop into an LLM for fine tuning (e.g., “Edit this into an email of <300 words, using the principles from [_The 15 Commitments of Conscious Leadership_](https://www.amazon.com/15-Commitments-Conscious-Leadership-Sustainable/dp/0990976904/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20)”).

bullets.section: What I’m watching again to prep for deeper work
bullets.title: Philip Roth: Unmasked
bullets.note: I greatly enjoyed this deep dive into the life, craft, and humor of Philip Roth. My quest to learn more about Philip was sparked by [Joyce Carol Oates](https://tim.blog/2021/02/10/joyce-carol-oates/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit), one of the most decorated and prodigious American writers of the last century, who spoke about him during [our podcast together](https://tim.blog/2021/02/10/joyce-carol-oates/?utm_campaign=5bf&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_source=convertkit). Here’s the official description of this interview-rich documentary: “American Masters explores the life and career of Pulitzer Prize- and National Book Award-winning novelist [Philip Roth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Roth), often referred to as the greatest living American writer. Reclusive and diffident, Roth grants very few interviews, but for the first time, allowed a journalist to spend 10 days interviewing him on camera.”
